messages:
From: Jason Liu <jason.liu@shopmidwest.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, SRE Team <sre@shopmidwest.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Dec 2026 08:15:34 -0800
Subject: Midwestern region - 503/504 spike, customers timing out

Hannah / Redwood team,

We're seeing a sustained increase in 502/503/504 responses and a ton of 429s from requests hitting the midwest edge (~us-east-2 fronting). Errors started at ~07:50 PST and have persisted. Our customers are reporting timeouts; several background jobs are failing with retry storms. I attached a small sample of edge logs and a heatmap from our side.

Key observations: 
- 50% of API requests to /v1/generate returning 503 in a 10m window.
- Clients are receiving 429s followed by retries that amplify load.
- Latency jumps before the errors, suggesting queue saturation at the LB or an upstream pool exhaustion.

We need an urgent mitigation plan and an ETA for a fix / fallback. If you want, we can open a bridge.

Attachments: midwest-edge-503-sample-logs.txt, midwest-traffic-heatmap.png

--
Jason Liu
SRE Lead, ShopMidwest

On it. Quick update:
- Short-term mitigation: enabling account-specific concurrency bump (+25%) and temporarily widening circuit-breaker windows for ShopMidwest only to reduce premature 429s. Applying a sticky routing override to prefer healthy pools in us-central for 20% of their traffic.
- Long-term: investigating whether our LB queue limits or connection pool sizing on the proxy tier needs tuning. Initial suspicion is an interaction between our autoscaler cooldown and sudden NUM_REQUESTS bursts.

Pinned commands / notes:
- Applied patch to routing ruleset: route_override(shopmidwest) -> prefer us-central for 20% of requests (will monitor).
- Pushed circuit-breaker adjustment: cb.window=30s -> 60s for account scope.

I will monitor Datadog for error rate and tail latency over the next 10 minutes and revert if any downstream instability.

Sean

Subject: Final update: Midwestern edge - stabilization, follow-ups, and next steps

Summary (what we did):
- Stabilized midwest edge by applying account-scoped routing override (20% traffic to us-central) and brief circuit-breaker window extension.
- Scaled up the upstream pool in us-east-2 by +3 instances where we observed high queue depth.
- Applied short-term token bucket rate smoothing to reduce retry amplification.

Impact observed:
- 503/504 rate for ShopMidwest dropped from 48% to 2.3% within 12 minutes of the mitigations.
- Client-side 429s decreased by ~70% over 15 minutes.

Next steps (owner / ETA):
- Root cause analysis: Sean/Jonas (72h) — investigate autoscaler cooldown interaction and LB queueing behavior.
- Postmortem & remediation plan: Hannah (96h) — will include regression tests and a new canary configuration for account-scoped routing.
- Customer credit proposal: Marissa (48h) — propose credit and communicate with ShopMidwest.

Attachments: runbook-circuit-breaker-snippet.txt

Thanks again for the quick triage, Jason. We will share the RCA and the datadog dashboards (public link) once the postmortem is complete. If you have any outstanding errors/screenshots please drop them into the PD incident (PD-INC-84721) or forward them to marissa_cole@redwood.ai.
